newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine banks cut prime lending rates.
newsitem.headline: Philippine banks cut prime lending rates.

text.p: Two of the largest banks in the country said on Thursday they had lowered their prime lending rates following the four percentage-point cut in the central bank's overnight borrowing rate to 28 percent.
An official of Far East Bank and Trust Co said the bank had cut its prime lending rate for new loans to 30/31 percent from 32 percent.
For old loans that would be repriced, the prime lending rate of Far East bank is lower at 28 percent from 32 percent, she said.
Banks of the Philippine Islands cut its prime lending rates on fresh availments to 29 percent from over 30 percent.
Its prime lending rates for repriced loans is lower at 26 percent from over 30 percent, a bank official said.
Banks had raised their prime lending rates after the central bank lifted its key overnight rate to a 2-1/2 year high last week to protect the peso.
As the currency market showed signs of normalisation on Wednesday, the central bank cut its rates effective on Thursday.

Central bank governor Gabriel Singson said the monetary authority might bring down overnight rates again after the peso rose substantially in midsession on Thursday to 27.65 to the dollar after it opened at 29.26.
